newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds down, focus on sterling.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds down, focus on sterling.

text.p: Irish government bonds were down in thin late trade on Thursday as the market kept a close eye on the currency markets and sterling in particular, dealers said.
"We have really seen the Irish market tread water, it is not doing a lot. We had outperformed over the last number of days but today we have seen a bit of retracement," one dealer said.
Traders said prices were roughly back to Monday's levels but added that they would not be surprised to see another push in the 10 to 15-year area.
"But for now the currencies are the main concern. We are watching to see if sterling will go as high as 2.80 against the mark and test 0.96 against the Irish," the dealer said.

By 1635 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 36 pence from Wednesday's close at 103.40 to yield 5.64 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 13 pence from the close at 111.20 to yield 6.38 pct.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 133 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 88 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.
The announcement that Moody's had upgraded the foreign-currency sovereign ceilings for bonds and bank deposits of Ireland from Aa2 to Aa1 had little impact on the market, economists said.
At the same, the rating agency confirmed its rating of Aaa on the government of Ireland's domestic-currency debt.
"It was fully expected that would happen given what they (Moody's) had said previously," Jim O'Leary, economist at Davy Stockbrokers, said. "They have merely re-affirmed what they had already said."
